questions.question: Which command gives a reproducible first check of this lesson's Rust entrypoint?
options: rustc --edition 2021 code/main.rs -o /tmp/env-check && /tmp/env-check
python3 code/main.rs
cargo add torch
Run nvidia-smi and assume it validates every language runtime
questions.explanation: The lesson is a standalone Rust program, so rustc compiles the file and the resulting binary runs the environment checks.

questions.question: What does parse_minor_python("Python 3.11.8") return?
options: None, because the version has three numeric components
questions.explanation: The helper removes the Python prefix, splits on periods, and parses the first two components as the major and minor versions.

questions.question: Why does main.rs check the four environment layers from the system upward?
options: AI libraries can install before their runtime exists
Rust only supports four installed programs
Upper layers depend on lower-layer tools
The order makes optional tools become required
questions.explanation: The program presents system foundation, package managers, runtimes, and AI libraries as dependent layers. A missing lower layer explains failures above it.

questions.question: A machine reports a passing NVIDIA driver in nvidia-smi, but torch.cuda.is_available() is False. What is the next useful check?
options: Rename the Python file to gpu.py
Increase the notebook font size
Delete the GPU driver so PyTorch can choose one
Install a compatible CUDA build and inspect torch.version.cuda
questions.explanation: nvidia-smi verifies the driver can see the device; PyTorch still needs a compatible CUDA build in the environment. Printing its CUDA build and reinstalling that environment if needed separates the two layers.

questions.question: The Rust report marks Python as failed with a version of Python 3.9. What should you fix before installing the AI libraries?
options: Install or select Python 3.10 or newer, then rerun the report
Make Julia a required check instead
Ignore the line because optional tools determine Python support
Compile the Rust binary with a different optimization level
questions.explanation: Python is a required check and the code rejects versions below 3.10. Fixing the runtime first prevents package installation from targeting an unsupported interpreter.

questions.question: You need to compare two machines before starting Phase 1. Which record is most useful?
options: A screenshot of the editor theme
Version lines, pass/fail counts, and a backend test result
The number of files in the home directory
Only the name of the installed AI framework
questions.explanation: The check is useful when it records the versions and pass/fail status for the required layers, plus a real backend operation. That evidence makes differences between machines actionable.
